newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No comment from Canberra on Telstra sale time.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No comment from Canberra on Telstra sale time.

text.p: Australian Acting Treasurer John Fahey declined on Thursday to provide details about the likely timing for the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp, saying only that there was a great deal of work to be done.
"Timing is not important. It's important to do it well and it's important to do it properly," Fahey told reporters.
"When that occurs the sale will proceed," he said.
Fahey said the government would consider a number of factors when planning the timing of the sale, including the state of the equity market.
"It will depend upon a number of factors and you can't pre-empt when those factors will come into place," he said.
"You can take advice, not the least being the state of the market and the degree of preparedness as we go down these various steps and fairly intense work over the next several months."
Fahey said the government was holding briefings on Thursday for 140 people interested in acting as the government's advisers on the sale.
"It is the first step of what will be a fairly long march through this process," he said.
Media analysts said last year the sale was unlikely to go ahead until the final quarter of 1997 at the earliest.
The government plans to raise A$8.0 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra.

The upper house of parliament, the Senate, has asked a committee to consider a proposal for the government to sell Telstra through redeemable preference shares. However, the government is expected to opt for the issue of ordinary shares.
The Senate committee will release its recommendation at the end of March.
